subject: Computer Networking
title: SMS, iMessage, and RCS
description: A short lesson to help you apply SMS, iMessage, and RCS.

hook.text: SMS is 30 years old and still works everywhere. But iMessage and RCS are replacing it piece by piece.

buildup.text: SMS travels over the cellular control channel. 160-character limit, no encryption, no read receipts.

discovery.text: iMessage uses Apple's servers with end-to-end encryption. Blue bubbles mean secure. Green means SMS fallback.

twist.text: RCS is the carrier-backed SMS upgrade. Rich media, typing indicators, and read receipts — but no E2E encryption.

climax.text: Google pushed RCS hard. Apple finally added RCS support in iOS 18 — green bubbles get upgrades at last.

punchline.text: SMS still works everywhere. RCS and iMessage make it richer.

quiz.question: What security feature does iMessage have that standard SMS lacks?

details.summary: SMS sends short text messages through the cellular network with no encryption. iMessage adds end-to-end encryption between Apple devices. RCS is the industry standard replacing SMS with features like read receipts, typing indicators, and media sharing, bringing SMS into the modern messaging era.
details.whyItMatters: The SMS to RCS evolution shows how messaging protocols must adapt. Understanding the differences explains why messages between Apple and Android devices have different capabilities.
takeaways: SMS is unencrypted and travels through the cellular network
iMessage provides end-to-end encryption for Apple-to-Apple messages
RCS replaces SMS with modern features across carriers

faq.question: Why are SMS messages not encrypted?
faq.answer: SMS was designed in the 1980s when security was not a priority. Messages travel as plain text through the cellular network and can be intercepted by carriers, law enforcement, or attackers. SMS was designed for short notifications, not private conversations.

faq.question: What does RCS add over SMS?
faq.answer: RCS adds read receipts, typing indicators, high-resolution media, group chats, reactions, and optionally end-to-end encryption. It uses data connections instead of the legacy carrier SMS system. RCS makes Android messaging competitive with iMessage features.
